title: Announcements and sending materials: ideas from other products
intro: This page covers announcements and sending materials inside a course for Essentials 2.0 (Semester, then Courses, then Announcements and send materials, then Shareable link). It is about how products solve the task, not how polished their screens look. Each example shows how another product lets someone running a course communicate from inside it. They announce to everyone or a group, or send selected files or links ahead of a session. They choose the channel (portal feed, email, shareable link, or Canvas as a learning management system (LMS)). They schedule it, and see who received or opened it. One section per question. Every card says what we would take from it. Weak examples are flagged. Sources are the design reference libraries Mobbin and Refero. We will cut the set down before showing it outside the team.

questions.title: How do products pick the audience, attach course materials, and schedule a send?
questions.answer: Every message editor in the set treats scheduling as part of the send, not as a separate feature. Slack puts presets and a custom date and time on the send-button menu. Whop uses an inline calendar menu. LinkedIn uses a clock icon. Basecamp uses 'Schedule and save'. Audience targeting is rarer and less detailed than expected. Google Classroom puts a 'For / All students' dropdown directly above the text box. Teachable offers everyone, a course, or an individual. The Leap uses named segments. Confluence only offers Public or Private plus a start and end window. Attachments are uploads in place (ClassDojo photo, Basecamp PDF, Whop image). Nobody attaches from a course library. Only The Leap closes the loop from recipients through confirmation to open and click stats. Confluence's one-active-banner limit is the caveat: a lasting materials banner and a timely one cannot both be on.

questions.title: How do products choose channels (in-app feed, email, push, link, external LMS), and is that one message editor or many features?
questions.answer: Two models show up. In 'one message editor, many channels', the channel is a control on the same post. beehiiv's Post, Email, Website and Delivery tabs roll into a per-channel recipient summary before sending. Kit adds a 'Publish to web' opt-in on top of a default email send. Intercom folds platform (web, iOS, Android) and push into one panel. In the 'implicit channel' model, the in-app post is the channel and the product only asks who is notified. Basecamp separates 'who should see this' from 'when I post this, notify…'. Substack bundles email and push into one default-on 'notify subscribers' toggle. Nobody in the set offers an external LMS as a channel inside the message editor; that lives in an export menu (see Q5). For a course, the useful split is visibility versus notification: the post is the record, and the channels are how people hear about it.

questions.title: How do products control shareable links (expiry, access level, revoke, tracking)?
questions.answer: Products put the link controls in one panel that answers five questions. Who can open (anyone, workspace, or specific people)? At what level (view, comment, or edit)? Until when, with which password, and how to revoke? Mural shows all five, including a timezone-stamped expiry and a 'Reset visitor link' that creates a new link rather than only turning the old one off. Proton has expiry, password and 'Stop sharing'. Notion turns relative presets ('in a week') into an exact date on the same screen and ends with a red Remove. Coda, Dropbox and Sketch focus on tiered access (workspace, guests, everyone) and per-person levels, with Copy link always in the same corner. Sketch splits public rights into download versus comment checkboxes. Only Loom shows tracking next to the share ('No views yet'). ClickUp is the weak example: expiry defaults to Never with no presets, no access level, and the only revoke is an all-or-nothing Unpublish.

questions.title: How do products show delivery feedback (sent, delivered, seen) and reminders?
questions.answer: Feedback is worth having only when it is per person and has an action next to it. Navan lists each invitee with a status, lets you select the non-responders, and offers 'Send a reminder' from the same table. Superhuman shows per-person, per-device, timestamped opens on the thread itself. Automation goes further: HoneyBook branches the follow-up on 'file viewed within 1 day'. Docusign lets you set the days before the first reminder and the repeat interval. Newsletter tools lead with totals (Mailchimp, HubSpot; Dub for link clicks) and keep per-recipient detail one tab away (Outseta's Recipients tab with last-opened timestamps). WhatsApp's Delivered and Read is the minimum: two statuses, one recipient. Square's Announcements list is the caution: a 'Seen by' column that shows nothing and offers no follow-up action.

questions.title: How do products hand content off to an external LMS (sign-in, map to a course, what is sent, confirmation)?
questions.answer: This is the thinnest question in the set and the most important one for Essentials. Only SchoolAI shows a complete hand-off. An Export menu lists Google Classroom next to Docs and PDF. A permission dialog says what will be shared. A sign-in permission step (OAuth) follows. A Class picker maps the document to one specific class. A short confirmation says 'Exported to Google Classroom!'. Course platforms in the set have no hand-off at all. In Kajabi, publishing inside the product is the send, so learners see the product's own portal. Generic connectors stop at authorization. Craft is a Connect and Disconnect toggle on a settings page. Cofounder's OAuth flow with per-scope toggles never reaches a 'what was sent' or success screen (a weak example). Nobody shows editing or syncing again later after the hand-off.

questions.title: How do learners receive announcements (feed, notification, email), and does that match the portal?
questions.answer: The consistent products give announcements a distinct type or place on the learner side. Microsoft Teams offers 'Post' versus 'Announcement' in the message editor and shows announcements with a bold title and replies attached. Circle routes them to an 'Announcements' space separate from the feed. ClassDojo keeps a teacher-only Pin so the post stays on top, with the attachment and replies in the same place. Unread items are gathered centrally in Slack's Activity screen rather than only inside the source channel. Spotify lets the recipient choose email versus push per category, a model for learner notification preferences. Coursera is the weak example. Instructor content sits in a 'Latest'-sorted Q&A list with no pin, no unread marker and no sender role. An announcement there looks the same as ordinary peer posts.

references.title: Basecamp message with schedule and PDF
references.question: Q1
references.take: Basecamp shows a message message editor with a PDF attached and a clock-icon schedule menu for date and time with 'Schedule and save'. This screen has no audience or notification controls.

references.title: ClassDojo new post with photo and schedule
references.question: Q1
references.take: ClassDojo opens a New Post dialog for one class. You can attach a photo, use optional AI writing help, then pick a calendar date and time. There is no audience picker because the class is the audience.

references.title: Confluence announcement banner setup
references.question: Q1
references.take: Confluence walks through an admin announcement banner: title, banner style, Public or Private audience, and an optional start and end date-time window with timezone. Only one banner can be active at a time.

references.title: Classroom announce box with audience picker
references.question: Q1
references.take: Google Classroom pairs a light 'Announce something to your class' text box with a 'For / All students' audience dropdown directly above it. Audience targeting can sit as one control next to the compose field instead of a separate step.

references.title: LinkedIn post with schedule dialog
references.question: Q1
references.take: LinkedIn puts a scheduling entry in the compose toolbar that opens a dedicated date-and-time picker before the post is queued. Scheduling can be an optional side dialog off the main message editor rather than a separate screen.

references.title: Slack schedule on the send button
references.question: Q1
references.take: On Slack, scheduling lives on the send button: a menu of presets or a custom date and time dialog with timezone. These steps do not show channel targeting or attachments.

references.title: Teachable broadcast email to a group
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable's announcement email message editor has a Send-to dropdown (everyone, a course, or an individual), plus subject and body. A confirm dialog follows, then a sent screen. No attachment is used.

references.title: The Leap broadcast with segments and confirm
references.question: Q1
references.take: The Leap's broadcast flow goes from a template chooser into a rich-text editor with a recipients dropdown for one or more contact segments. It then forces a review-and-confirm dialog before send, and finishes on a sent screen with immediate analytics. That pairs audience targeting with an explicit confirm step in a course message editor.

references.title: Whop announcement with calendar schedule
references.question: Q1
references.take: Whop's message editor embeds an image and uses an inline calendar menu to switch the main action between publish now and scheduled. There is no audience control.

references.title: Basecamp who sees vs who is notified
references.question: Q2
references.take: Basecamp uses one message-board message editor that separates 'Who should see this?' (team only versus allow client) from 'When I post this, notify…' (requester, everyone I select, or no one). The in-app post is the channel.

references.title: beehiiv delivery tabs and recipient summary
references.question: Q2
references.take: beehiiv's Delivery tab sits on a single post with Post, Email, Website and SEO tabs. It shows segment exclusions, a web-access toggle and a per-channel recipient summary (Email: 6, Web: all free subscribers) before Schedule or Send.

references.title: Intercom message platforms and push
references.question: Q2
references.take: Intercom's Content tab mixes reply type (chat versus email collector), platform (Web, iOS, Android) and a mobile push toggle in one panel. Audience routing is not on this screen.

references.title: Kit broadcast with publish-to-web toggle
references.question: Q2
references.take: Kit's broadcast message editor has an audience filter builder and a send-time field that defaults to 'Send now'. A 'Publish to web' toggle adds an extra channel on top of the default email.

references.title: Substack publish with notify toggle
references.question: Q2
references.take: Substack's iOS publish dialog shows audience (who can view), a notification delivery toggle for email and push, and send controls.

references.title: ClickUp public link expiry set to Never
references.question: Q3
references.take: ClickUp's Public tab on the share sheet shows a public link and 'Expire link after: Never' with no presets. It also has a search-engine toggle, per-field visibility toggles, and Unpublish as the only, all-or-nothing revoke.

references.title: Coda share dialog with access modes
references.question: Q3
references.take: Coda shows a full share flow: access mode (anyone or specific people), recipient selection, copy link, and permission confirmation in a document sharing dialog.

references.title: Dropbox share link and add people
references.question: Q3
references.take: Dropbox's share dialog has an 'Anyone with this link: can edit' dropdown, add-person-by-email with a note, and Copy link. Expiration and password sit behind an unopened Settings link.

references.title: Loom share with per-person access list
references.question: Q3
references.take: Loom's Share dialog lets the owner add a person or Space and set a permission level (for example 'Can view') before sending the invite. The person then appears in an invited access list. That shows who currently has access, not only how to generate a link.

references.title: Mural link access, expiry and reset
references.question: Q3
references.take: Mural's access and settings panel shows restricted or general access, visitor link controls, an expiration date, a password, and a reset visitor link button.

references.title: Notion link level, expiry and remove
references.question: Q3
references.take: Notion's iOS link access dialog shows access level options (can edit, can comment, can view). It also has link expiration with time presets (1 hour, 1 day, 1 week) and a remove access option.

references.title: Proton share link expiry and password
references.question: Q3
references.take: Proton's settings dialog for a shared link has an expiration date field, a password requirement toggle, and a stop sharing option to revoke access.

references.title: Sketch share tiers and public rights
references.question: Q3
references.take: Sketch's share dialog has three access tiers (Workspace members, Guests, Everyone). The public-link tier has a view-or-no-access choice plus separate Inspect-and-download and Comment checkboxes, with Copy Link fixed top-right.

references.title: Docusign auto reminders setup
references.question: Q4
references.take: Docusign's advanced reminder setup covers expiration date, recipient privileges, an auto-reminder toggle, days before the first reminder, repeat interval, and a custom number of days.

references.title: Dub link clicks and trend chart
references.question: Q4
references.take: Dub's Analytics view shows Clicks, Leads and Sales counters plus a time-series chart for links filtered by tag. Link-level delivery feedback can be a few totals and a trend line rather than a per-recipient log of who clicked.

references.title: HoneyBook viewed-within-a-day follow-up
references.question: Q4
references.take: HoneyBook's workflow setup sends an email, waits one day, checks whether the file was viewed in that period, then branches to different follow-up emails.

references.title: HubSpot campaign totals only
references.question: Q4
references.take: HubSpot's Campaign Analyze tab shows aggregate metrics only (Sent, Delivered rate, Open, Click, Reply rate, bounce, unsubscribe, spam). There is no per-recipient list or action on this screen.

references.title: Mailchimp campaign counts and recipients
references.question: Q4
references.take: Mailchimp's campaign analytics overview shows three recipients plus delivered, clicked, bounced and unsubscribed counts. A recipient activity tab tracks open and click per recipient.

references.title: Navan remind non-responders from a list
references.question: Q4
references.take: Navan's flow shows invite creation, reminder selection from the invite list, and confirmation to send a reminder email to selected non-responders.

references.title: Outseta recipients with last opened
references.question: Q4
references.take: Outseta's Recipients tab for a sent broadcast has one row per recipient with Last opened, Clicked and Unsubscribed timestamps, plus status filters (Opened, Clicked, Bounced) and Export. There is no resend action on this screen.

references.title: Square announcements with empty Seen by
references.question: Q4
references.take: Square's Announcements list has a Status column (Sent) and a separate 'Seen by' column that is empty for the row shown. The field exists without data and without a follow-up action.

references.title: Superhuman who opened the mail
references.question: Q4
references.take: Superhuman's mail view shows team read statuses with an opened or unopened indicator. June and Perry have opened, and the view shows who has opened messages.

references.title: WhatsApp delivered and read info
references.question: Q4
references.take: WhatsApp's per-message info screen has two statuses, Read and Delivered, each with a timestamp. That is the minimum useful feedback for a single recipient, with no further breakdown.

references.title: Cofounder OAuth connect without success
references.question: Q5
references.take: Cofounder's OAuth connect flow for cross-posting covers a destination picker, per-scope permission toggles, a 'continue sharing?' re-consent screen, then a loading screen. The flow ends before showing what was sent or any success screen.

references.title: Craft connect and disconnect toggles
references.question: Q5
references.take: Craft's settings page lists integrations (Figma, GitHub, Jira, Linear) with a bare Connect or Disconnect toggle. There is no destination, no content, and no confirmation of anything sent.

references.title: Kajabi publish module as the send
references.question: Q5
references.take: Kajabi changes a curriculum module from Draft to Published and shows 'Successfully updated module' as a short confirmation. In a course platform, publishing is the send and there is no external hand-off.

references.title: SchoolAI export to Google Classroom
references.question: Q5
references.take: SchoolAI shows a complete external hand-off. An Export menu lists Google Classroom next to Docs and PDF. A permission dialog says what will be shared. An OAuth enable step follows. A Class picker maps the document to one class. A short confirmation confirms the export.

references.title: Circle Announcements space in the sidebar
references.question: Q6
references.take: Circle's sidebar lists 'Announcements' as its own space separate from 'Feed', with a notification bell in the header. Admin announcements have a dedicated place instead of mixing into ordinary posts.

references.title: ClassDojo pinned teacher announcement
references.question: Q6
references.take: ClassDojo shows a teacher-posted course announcement to families with rich text, imagery, likes and comments. That is how learners receive the post on their side.

references.title: Coursera Latest discussion list
references.question: Q6
references.take: Coursera's mobile discussion list sorted by Latest mixes a bug report, a technical question and a lecture question with no pin, unread marker or sender role. An announcement dropped here would look the same as ordinary peer posts.

references.title: Teams announcement post in a channel
references.question: Q6
references.take: Microsoft Teams shows a team channel announcement post with metadata, replies and engagement options. Learners can see course updates as a distinct post type.

references.title: Slack Activity inbox on mobile
references.question: Q6
references.take: Slack's mobile Activity inbox gathers notifications and mentions in one place. Learners can receive course announcements from a central inbox rather than only inside each channel.

references.title: Spotify per-category email and push
references.question: Q6
references.take: Spotify's Notification settings list content categories (Music, Podcasts, Audiobooks, Concerts, Livestreams), each with its own Email and Push checkboxes. A learner-facing portal could let people set per-category channel preferences for course communications the same way.
